label: original-phase input of x/m/3/g/t (first or second such token)
predicate: (phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("x"), tok("m"), tok("3"), tok("g"), tok("t")]) & (n_seen([tok("x"), tok("m"), tok("3"), tok("g"), tok("t")]) <= 1)
explanation: 96% of activation mass is in the original (input) phase. It never fires at the delimiter and fires only weakly in the copy phase. It is driven by the identity of the current input token: x (rate 34%), m (31%), 3 (30%), g (17%) and t (13%), with weaker firing on s, v, i and e. Rates are highest at t=0..5 and drop off after t~6. Activation is weaker when the token is a repeat (in_first=0) or when several tokens from this set have already appeared. The strongest activations (near max) are on x/3/m right after a prefix of c/d/k tokens (e.g. c c d x). It barely fires on tokens such as b, h and u. The token-set predicate plateaus around dev F1 0.59 (mass recall 0.78), and refinements by position or prior context did not get past that. The rest of the variation looks like a graded function of the token and its context, not a crisp rule.
